spherical_capacity_kappa0.cite: Gardner, J. Phys. A 21, 257 (1988) and Cover, IEEE Trans. Electron. Comput. 14, 326 (1965) (originals not fetched); value read from Gyorgyi, arXiv:cond-mat/0010025, Sec. II E 1 ('alpha_c = Mc/N ... approaches, with probability 1, the value alpha_c = 2'), from Franz & Parisi, arXiv:1501.03397, Eq. (2) and text ('alpha(0) = 2'), and from Pastore, Rotondo, Erba & Gherardi, arXiv:2005.10002, Eq. (17) (alpha_c = 2 from Cover's theorem). Convention: J.J = N, constraint J.xi/sqrt(N) >= kappa, kappa = 0
spherical_capacity_kappa0.independent_route: (1) Cover's count of separable dichotomies by its recurrence C(N,p+1) = C(N,p) + C(N-1,p) in exact integers (no replicas, no closed form): the separable fraction is exactly 1/2 at p = 2N and a steepening sigmoid around alpha = 2; (2) replicant's own RS saddle parametrised by q, alpha(q) = q/((1-q) E[(phi/H)^2]), evaluated at q -> 1

ising_rs_capacity.cite: Gardner & Derrida, J. Phys. A 21, 271 (1988) (original not fetched); read from Gyorgyi, arXiv:cond-mat/0010025, Sec. II E 2: 'The RS solution formally exists beyond the transition and stays locally, i. e., AT-stable up to alpha = 4/pi'. The paper states the closed form 4/pi; value = its decimal. Gyorgyi's 'AT-stable up to 4/pi' is NOT reproduced by replicant (our replicon turns negative near alpha = 1.015, see families/perceptron.py); the q -> 1 endpoint 4/pi itself is reproduced
ising_rs_capacity.independent_route: replicant's own RS saddle of the Ising volume parametrised by qhat (q = E tanh^2(sqrt(qhat) z), alpha(qhat) = qhat (1-q)/E[(phi/H)^2], explicit, no root finding) climbs towards it as qhat -> infinity (tests at qhat = 1e2, 1e3, 1e4); the closed form (2/pi)/int_{-kappa}^inf Dt (t+kappa)^2 is our own q -> 1 asymptotics

ising_1rsb_capacity.cite: Krauth & Mezard, J. Phys. France 50, 3057 (1989) (original not fetched; quoted as 'alpha_c ~ 0.833' in Gyorgyi, arXiv:cond-mat/0010025, Sec. II E 2, and in Huang, arXiv:2404.18902). Digits read from Ding & Sun, arXiv:1809.07742, Eq. (153): alpha_lb = 0.833078599, alpha_ub = 0.833078600 bracket the Krauth-Mezard alpha_* (root of the RS entropy G_*(alpha), their Prop. 1.3); value = bracket midpoint, tol = bracket half-width rounded up. Conventions: J in {-1,+1}^N, Gaussian patterns, kappa = 0
ising_1rsb_capacity.independent_route: replicant's own frozen-1RSB solve: with q1 = 1 the 1RSB volume is S_RS(q0)/m, stationary in m only where S_RS = 0, so alpha_c is the root of replicant's RS entropy, found by secant on the saddle parametrised by qhat (does not use the paper's number); plus exact small-N enumeration (N = 11, 13), statistical and finite-size, which excludes the RS value 4/pi

ising_1rsb_q.cite: Ding & Sun, arXiv:1809.07742, Eq. (153): q_lb = 0.56394907949, q_ub = 0.56394908030 bracket q_*(alpha_*), the RS overlap at the Krauth-Mezard threshold; value = midpoint, tol = half-width rounded up
ising_1rsb_q.independent_route: replicant's own RS saddle at its own root of the RS entropy (gardner_capacity('ising', ansatz='1rsb').point.q)

ising_1rsb_qhat.cite: Ding & Sun, arXiv:1809.07742, Eq. (153): psi_lb = 2.5763513100, psi_ub = 2.5763513224 bracket psi_* = R(q_*, alpha_*), the conjugate field (our qhat) at the Krauth-Mezard threshold; value = midpoint, tol = half-width rounded up
ising_1rsb_qhat.independent_route: replicant's own RS saddle at its own root of the RS entropy (gardner_capacity('ising', ansatz='1rsb').point.qhat)

gibbs_asymptotic_constant.cite: Seung, Sompolinsky & Tishby, Phys. Rev. A 45, 6056 (1992) (original not fetched); read from Buhot, Torres Moreno & Gordon, arXiv:cond-mat/9703183, Sec. I: Gibbs generalization error 'vanishes ... like eps_g ~ 0.625/alpha [1]', [1] = Seung et al. Meaning: lim alpha * eps_Gibbs(alpha). tol = 3-digit rounding
gibbs_asymptotic_constant.independent_route: replicant's own RS saddle R/sqrt(1-R) = (alpha/pi) int Dt exp(-R t^2/2)/H(-sqrt(R) t), solved at alpha = 100, 1000: alpha * arccos(R)/pi approaches the closed form sqrt(2)/I, I = int Dt exp(-t^2/2)/H(-t) (our own large-alpha expansion, 0.624658...)

bayes_asymptotic_constant.cite: Opper & Haussler, Phys. Rev. Lett. 66, 2677 (1991) (original not fetched); read from Buhot, Torres Moreno & Gordon, arXiv:cond-mat/9703183, Sec. I: 'the bayesian generalization error vanishes like eps_g ~ 0.442/alpha, in the limit of large alpha'; their Eq. (15a) is the Gibbs equation with R_Gibbs = R_Bayes^2 (citing Opper & Haussler). tol = 3-digit rounding
bayes_asymptotic_constant.independent_route: replicant: R_Bayes = sqrt(R_Gibbs) on our own Gibbs saddle, alpha * arccos(sqrt(R))/pi at alpha = 100, 1000 approaches the closed form 1/I (0.441700...)

margin_law_collapse.cite: INTERNAL IDENTITY, not a literature number.  Gaussian margin offset kappa_l = mu + s g (g ~ N(0,1) quenched): at q -> 1 alpha_c(law) = 1/E_g D(mu + s g) = alpha_c^catalog(kappa~)/(1 + s^2), kappa~ = mu/sqrt(1 + s^2), D(k) = (1 + k^2) H(-k) + k phi(k). In the (a, h) form of constraints a g_l + b y_l <= h, a^2 + b^2 = 1: alpha_eff = alpha/(1 - a^2), kappa~ = -h. Derived in tools/replicant/families/margin_law.py (module docstring) and stated, with the same collapse, in the manuscript limit-fig2-paper main.tex, Appendix 'Replica theory for random documents', paragraph 'Reduction to a perceptron' (Eq. gardner and the sentence 'Since a g - b z is itself a standard Gaussian...'; read, local manuscript, not published). The banked number is the residual |alpha_c(law)(1 + s^2) - alpha_c^catalog(kappa~)| at mu = -0.5, s = 0.75 (kappa~ = -0.4, alpha_c ~ 2.54). tol 1e-13 covers float rounding at the default 15 digits (the test battery checks 1e-15 at 20 digits for eight (a, h) pairs)
margin_law_collapse.independent_route: law_capacity integrates E_kappa D(kappa) over the Gaussian law by tanh-sinh quadrature in g and never uses the collapse; gardner_capacity('spherical', kappa~) is the closed form 1/D(kappa~); a third route, the unmerged two-dimensional (t, g) Gauss-Hermite alpha(q) of families/margin_law.alpha_unmerged, and a fourth, finite-N least-norm sampling (numerics/margin_perceptron.py), are in tests/test_margin_law.py

spherical_1rsb_capacity_kappa_m2p7.cite: Stojnic, 'Fl RDT based ultimate lowering of the negative spherical perceptron capacity', arXiv:2312.16531 (v1, Dec 2023), read from the arXiv PDF (pdftotext of the downloaded file, tables read as text) Table 2 (second full level of lifting, 2-sfl RDT; the capacity column alpha at kappa = -2.7): 942.9. Convention: alpha_c(kappa) is the storage capacity of the spherical perceptron with margin kappa < 0 (J.xi/sqrt(N) >= kappa, J.J = N), his alpha_c = [int_{-kappa}^inf Dz (z+kappa)^2]^-1 at the first level (1-sfl, his Table 3 row 1 = 13.27 at kappa = -1, equal to replicant's RS value). That his r-sfl RDT level r+1 equals the r-step RSB jamming capacity of this package is our identification, found numerically here (it agrees at ten kappa to 6.2e-4 relative; he does not state it). He gives a rigorous-bound derivation (fully lifted random duality theory) and prints 4 significant digits from a numerical optimisation; his values lie at or above replicant's (as a numerically optimised upper bound does), tol = 1e-3 relative.
spherical_1rsb_capacity_kappa_m2p7.independent_route: replicant's own 1RSB jamming point: the minimum of A(mu, q0) = -ent/en over the zero-temperature scaling limit (1 - q1 = delta -> 0, m = mu delta) of the 1RSB entropy of Franz, Parisi, Sevelev, Urbani & Zamponi, SciPost Phys. 2, 019 (2017), arXiv:1702.06919, Eq. (59) (families/perceptron_rsb.py, mpmath, audited); no number or parameter of Stojnic's paper enters. Cross-checks in tests/test_perceptron_rsb.py: the scaling limit of the unscaled entropy, and the integer-n replica functional (n = 4, m = 2) against a Gaussian orthant probability
